classification.difficultyReason: Determine circle equations from intercepts or circumference coordinates, using Pythagoras where required.

content.prompt: Determine the equation of each circle. They are all centred at the origin.

spec.description: Origin-centred circle with positive-end axis arrows and labelled intercepts; no grid or tick marks.
spec.answerVisibility: All intercept givens are permanent; equation is answer-only.

spec.description: Circle, point (5,12), radius r, dashed vertical projection and right-angle mark. Empty leg-label boxes remain associated with their horizontal and vertical sides.
spec.mathematics: Point (5,12) lies on a circle centred at (0,0); perpendicular foot is (5,0).
spec.answerVisibility: Point and radius label are permanent. Both leg boxes are empty in Questions.

answer.worked:
The triangle legs have lengths $5$ and $12$.
$$\begin{aligned}r^2&=5^2+12^2\\r^2&=25+144=169\\x^2+y^2&=169\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Circle, point (−7,24), arrowed radius r, dashed vertical projection and right-angle mark. Horizontal response box below the negative x-axis; vertical response box left of the projection.
spec.mathematics: Point (−7,24) lies on an origin-centred circle; perpendicular foot is (−7,0).
spec.answerVisibility: Coordinates and r are givens; both leg boxes remain empty.

answer.worked:
The triangle legs have lengths $7$ and $24$.
$$\begin{aligned}r^2&=7^2+24^2\\r^2&=49+576=625\\x^2+y^2&=625\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Circle, point (20,−21), arrowed radius r, dashed vertical projection and right-angle mark. Horizontal response box above the positive x-axis; vertical response box right of the projection.

answer.worked:
